stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Pick each of the four filter families and drag the cutoff slider. Watch how the Bode magnitude curve reshapes: flat then falling for low-pass, rising then flat for high-pass, a peak for band-pass, a notch for band-stop. Advance after sampling at least $3$ families.
stages.concept: A linear filter is described by its complex transfer function $H(j\omega) = V_s/V_e$. Its magnitude $|H(f)|$ tells which bands are passed and which are attenuated: **low-pass** keeps $f < f_c$; **high-pass** keeps $f > f_c$; **band-pass** keeps a window around $f_0$; **band-stop** rejects a window around $f_0$. On a $\log_{10}(f)$ axis the shapes are distinctive — that is why we plot $|H|_{\text{dB}}$ against $\log_{10}(f)$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Now build a specific low-pass with two components. Adjust $R$ and $C$ so the cutoff $f_c$ lands on the dashed orange target ($1\,\text{kHz}$). Many $(R, C)$ pairs work — you need $R\,C = 1/(2\pi\,f_c)$.
stages.concept: For the RC low-pass, $H(j\omega) = 1/(1 + j\,R\,C\,\omega)$, so $|H(f)| = 1/\sqrt{1 + (f/f_c)^2}$ with $f_c = 1/(2\pi\,R\,C)$. At $f = f_c$ the gain drops to $1/\sqrt{2}$ ($-3\,\text{dB}$). For $f_c = 1\,\text{kHz}$: $R\,C \approx 1.59 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{s}$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The schematic is hidden. Only the Bode magnitude curve is shown. Classify each filter as low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, or band-stop. Answer every question correctly in one pass — a wrong answer restarts the deck.
stages.concept: Classification cues on $|H|_{\text{dB}}$ vs $\log_{10}(f)$: **low-pass** — flat at $0\,\text{dB}$ on the left, drops on the right; **high-pass** — rises on the left, flat at $0\,\text{dB}$ on the right; **band-pass** — peaks near $f_0$ and falls on both sides; **band-stop** — flat then dips sharply near $f_0$ and rises again.

labels.question: question
labels.evaluate_prompt: Classify the filter from its Bode magnitude curve.
labels.tip1: each family has a distinct silhouette — flip through the four
labels.tip2: R↑ or C↑ → f_c shifts left ;  f_c = 1/(2π·R·C)
labels.tip3: read the low-f side then the high-f side — flat vs sloped
labels.peek_tip_1: Look at the low-frequency end first. Is |H| flat at 0 dB (passes low f) or falling (rejects low f)?
labels.peek_tip_2: Now the high-frequency end. Flat = passes high f. Falling = rejects high f. Combine both ends to name the family.
labels.peek_tip_3: A single dip in the middle = band-stop. A single peak in the middle = band-pass. No dip and no peak = low- or high-pass.

1.1: Click one of the four family buttons and drag the cutoff slider — the curve reshapes.
1.2: Compare low-pass (drops on the right) vs high-pass (drops on the left). Then band-pass (peak) vs band-stop (notch).
1.3: You need to visit 3 different families. The counter in the top-right tracks progress.

2.1: You need R·C = 1/(2π·1000) ≈ 1.59×10⁻⁴ s. Pick a round C, then compute R.
2.3: Or C = 10 nF with R = 16 kΩ. Or C = 1 µF with R = 160 Ω — all give f_c ≈ 1 kHz.

3.1: Scan the two ends of the curve. Low end flat + high end drops = low-pass. Reverse = high-pass.
3.2: A single peak (curve arcs up in the middle) = band-pass. A single dip (curve plunges in the middle) = band-stop.
3.3: Ignore the exact frequency. Only the silhouette matters here — flat / slope / peak / notch.
